# The board

> Every request to the editor and every task on SHarness, numbered, with its owner and its status; one file per row.

*Source: <https://sharness.ai/admin/board/index.html> · generated by tools/gen_admin.py from content/admin/, so the page and this file cannot drift. Every page on this site has a .md twin.*

---

Every piece of work on SHarness as one row, numbered so it can be referred to from any page, commit or conversation, and never renumbered. **R** is a request: it needs the editor (a decision, a key, a setting) and says what it blocks. **T** is a task: work a member has or anyone can pick up. One file per row under `content/admin/board/`; the [Sherpa](../members/sherpa/index.md) keeps the rows honest and scopes them into releases, the [conductor](../members/conductor/index.md) builds this page from them, and anyone opens a row by adding a file ([how](../guidance/index.md)). 13 request(s) wait on the editor and 12 task(s) are open, as of 26 Oct 2026.

| R15 | **Set the repository and account settings on the security lock-down list (branch rulesets, 2FA, push protection, the PyPI publisher bound to an environment).** The security review of 25 Oct 2026 ([Reviews](../../security/reviews/index.md), register row [SR-24](../../security/risks/index.md#the-register)) found `main` and `dev` of both repositories unprotected, one account administering both, and a push to the CLI's `main` publishing to PyPI. Nothing in a repository can change these; [Hardening §3](../../security/hardening/index.md#3-the-repositories-and-the-accounts-settings-only-a-person-can-change) is the checklist, with the weight of each item: two-factor for the organisation; branch rulesets on `main` and `dev` requiring a pull request and the `tests`, `security` and `codeql` checks, blocking force pushes and deletion; a tag ruleset for `v*`; secret scanning with push protection; Dependabot alerts; private vulnerability reporting; the Trusted Publisher on PyPI bound to a `pypi` environment with a required reviewer; Pages deploying only from Actions and only from `dev` and `main`. One decision inside it: the release workflow pushes a version-bump commit to `main`, which a ruleset blocks unless the Actions actor is on its bypass list; the alternative is to derive the version from the tag in the build job and never commit it from CI. The editor sets these and ticks them; the security agent confirms what the API shows afterwards. (opened 2026-10-26) | editor | open |
| R16 | **Decide the environment row for the policy (process.env), so a confined child stops inheriting every variable of the process that confined it.** Register row [SR-11](../../security/risks/index.md#the-register): today `sharness-ai run` passes the whole environment of the applying process to the child, API keys and proxy credentials included, because v0 has no row for it; since 25 Oct 2026 `run` says so on stderr every time and `policy check` in its advice. Proposed for the next policy version: `process.env` taking `"inherit"`, `"clean"` or a list of variable names to pass. A new optional key leaves every existing hash unchanged; a CLI without the key refuses the unknown key, which is the right failure. The designed end state removes most of the need (`sharness.llm` and `sharness.kms` hold the secrets), but the row is cheap and closes a Medium gap now. The editor decides the shape; the security agent implements it with a test and the hash fixtures. (opened 2026-10-26) | editor | open |

| T14 | **The row shape in policy.py, so that policy check derives the barrier kind per row.** From [the PBP on one page](../../design/pbp/index.md) §4 and §5: a policy row is subject, resource, operation, predicate (`where`), `held_by` and a derived `kind`. `sharness-ai policy check` should compute, for every behaviour row, whether its preconditions hold (the capability rows close every other path to the resource; one edge to the keeper) and report the barrier kind: Boundary when they do, Expectation when they do not, never an error. The summary then counts rows held by the kernel, rows held by a keeper and rows unheld, beside `hello`'s probes held. Opened by sharness.pbp, who writes the shape; sharness.build or sharness.dev write the code. The first predicate to carry is `append_only`, because `sharness.fs` is its keeper in the design. (opened 2026-10-25) | sharness.build | open |
